exposure: Socioeconomic status (higher vs. urban economic poverty)
cohort: The study included 2,523 unique patient deliveries from a large hospital network in New York, corresponding to conceptions that occurred during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown, serving a racially and socioeconomically diverse population.
finding: During the initial COVID-19 lockdown in New York, there was a 22.85% decrease in births compared to the same period the previous year, with most of this decline attributable to fewer births among individuals of higher socioeconomic status.
cross-section timing: Births corresponding to conceptions during the COVID-19 pandemic lockdown (March 22, 2020 onwards) compared to the same period in the previous year.
